variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Neural architecture search (NAS) is the practice of using an optimization system to propose, evaluate, and select neural network structures under explicit deployment constraints. Instead of manually fixing every layer, width, connection, and operation, engineers define a legal search space and an evidence protocol that compares candidate architectures.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Declare the deployment envelope
pairs.detail: Set quality floors, p95 latency, memory, energy, throughput, hardware, compiler, training budget, and prohibited operations.
pairs.explanation: Set quality floors, p95 latency, memory, energy, throughput, hardware, compiler, training budget, and prohibited operations.

pairs.label: Define a legal search space
pairs.detail: Choose operations, connections, depth, width, scaling rules, and shape constraints that can be built and measured consistently.
pairs.explanation: Choose operations, connections, depth, width, scaling rules, and shape constraints that can be built and measured consistently.

pairs.label: Propose the next candidates
pairs.detail: Use evolution, Bayesian optimization, reinforcement learning, or a differentiable relaxation to allocate evaluation budget.
pairs.explanation: Use evolution, Bayesian optimization, reinforcement learning, or a differentiable relaxation to allocate evaluation budget.

pairs.label: Measure a comparable proxy
pairs.detail: Train or inherit candidate weights under one versioned protocol and record quality, cost, failures, and hardware measurements.
pairs.explanation: Train or inherit candidate weights under one versioned protocol and record quality, cost, failures, and hardware measurements.

pairs.label: Update the Pareto frontier
pairs.detail: Retain candidates that are not dominated across quality, latency, memory, energy, robustness, and uncertainty.
pairs.explanation: Retain candidates that are not dominated across quality, latency, memory, energy, robustness, and uncertainty.

pairs.label: Retrain finalists independently
pairs.detail: Start from fresh initialization, repeat seeds, use full data and budget, and validate on target hardware and untouched test evidence.
pairs.explanation: Start from fresh initialization, repeat seeds, use full data and budget, and validate on target hardware and untouched test evidence.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Neural architecture search (NAS) is the practice of using an optimization system to propose, evaluate, and select neural network structures under explicit deployment constraints. Instead of manually fixing every layer, width, connection, and operation, engineers define a legal search space and an evidence protocol that compares candidate architectures.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Regularized evolution
pairs.detail: Mutates strong candidates while retiring old population members.
pairs.explanation: Mutates strong candidates while retiring old population members. It parallelizes well and handles discrete spaces, but may require many evaluations.

pairs.label: Bayesian optimization
pairs.detail: Fits a surrogate over architecture encodings and acquisition objectives.
pairs.explanation: Fits a surrogate over architecture encodings and acquisition objectives. It can spend fewer expensive evaluations when the surrogate is informative.

pairs.label: Differentiable search
pairs.detail: Relaxes operation choices into continuous weights and trains a supernet.
pairs.explanation: Relaxes operation choices into continuous weights and trains a supernet. Discretization and weight-sharing bias require independent confirmation.

pairs.label: Reinforcement learning
pairs.detail: Trains a controller from candidate rewards.
pairs.explanation: Trains a controller from candidate rewards. It is flexible but often expensive, high variance, and sensitive to reward design.

variants.context: Neural architecture search (NAS) is the practice of using an optimization system to propose, evaluate, and select neural network structures under explicit deployment constraints. Instead of manually fixing every layer, width, connection, and operation, engineers define a legal search space and an evidence protocol that compares candidate architectures.
variants.prompt: What is the core evidence invariant of NAS?
options: Candidates must use comparable versioned scoring, and finalists must be retrained independently of the search proxy
Every candidate must inherit the same weights
The largest search space always wins
Wall time and accelerator-hours are identical
variants.explanation: Comparable evidence prevents protocol drift, while independent retraining tests whether proxy or weight-sharing conditions created the apparent winner.
